key_insight: A Taguchi L9 design showed that wire feed rate is the dominant driver of tensile strength in GMAW mild-steel welds, with the best performance near 26 V, 184.33 A, and 220 m/min.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical parameter-setting guide for improving weld strength in automated steel fabrication while reducing trial-and-error tuning.
method: Used an L9 orthogonal array to test three GMAW inputs at three levels each.
Evaluated tensile strength with signal-to-noise ratio and ANOVA.
Ranked factor influence: wire feed rate > welding current > arc voltage.
evidence_signal: ANOVA attributed 34.64% of the variation to wire feed rate, 19.42% to current, and 5.95% to arc voltage, and the best experimental trial reached 688 MPa tensile strength.
watch_item: The optimum is based on a limited nine-run Taguchi setup on ST-37 mild steel, so transfer to other materials, joint geometries, or welding systems should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Optimization of Gas Metal Arc Welding Process Parameters for Enhanced Tensile Strength of Mild Steel Weldments Using the Taguchi Design of Experiments and Analysis of Variance
